title: Peat Inventory of Minnesota
abstract: Reconnaissance- and detailed-level peatland survey data for Minnesota, compiled by the Minnesota DNR beginning in 1976 and expanded with U.S. Department of Energy funding from 1979, to determine the dimensions, quantity, quality, type, and depth of major peat deposits. Linked tables record site locations, peatland vegetation and classification, peat profile descriptions (peat type/classification, depth, degree of decomposition on the von Post scale, botanical origin), and DNR and DOE Coal Analysis Laboratory analytical results (bulk density, moisture, pH, ash content, heating value, proximate/ultimate analysis) for individual peat inventory sites across 21 Minnesota counties. Field survey reports and maps for four study areas (Aitkin, Beltrami-Lake of the Woods, Koochiching, and southwest St. Louis counties) were published 1979-1982; reports were later scanned to PDF and maps rectified for GIS use.
source_org: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources (DNR); distributed via Minnesota Geospatial Commons (State of Minnesota / MnGeo)
source_citation: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. Peat Inventory of Minnesota. Minnesota Geospatial Commons, State of Minnesota. Published March 11, 2019. https://gis.data.mn.gov/datasets/173d3993a9f2433bb093c970ac3e8d38_0/about
geo_description: Northern, central, and east-central Minnesota. Sites recorded in 21 counties per Locate.csv: Aitkin, Beltrami, Benton, Carlton, Cass, Chisago, Clearwater, Crow Wing, Hubbard, Isanti, Itasca, Kanabec, Kittson, Koochiching, Lake, Lake of the Woods, Marshall, Mille Lacs, Pine, Roseau, St. Louis.
spatial_reference: UTM Zone 15N; NAD83 (UTM_E83/UTM_N83/UTM_Z83 fields in Locate.csv), with legacy NAD27 coordinates also present (UTM_E27/UTM_N27/UTM_Z27)
license: Custom License (per Minnesota Geospatial Commons item page); full license text not included in supplied materials
intellectual_rights: Minnesota Geospatial Commons lists this item as 'Public - Anyone can see this content' under a 'Custom License' with a 'View license details' link. The full license text was not part of the supplied source material and has not been reviewed.
methods_summary: Reconnaissance-level surveys (broad, random/traverse locations) and later detailed-level, grid-based surveys. Crews recorded peatland vegetation, peat type through the profile, peat depth, and collected samples. Von Post degree-of-decomposition (H1-H10) correlated to USDA SCS Fibric (H1-H3) / Hemic (H4-H6) / Sapric (H7-H10) classes (VonPost.csv). Samples analyzed by DNR laboratory (bulk density, moisture, pH, ash content - Labdnr.csv) and DOE Coal Analysis Laboratory (proximate: Btu/lb, volatiles, fixed carbon - Labprox.csv; ultimate: total carbon, H, N, S, O - Labulti.csv). Source: MnGeo landing-page summary; TablesInPeat.csv.
processing_summary: Lab acquired 11 CSV exports (BotanicalOrigin, Labdnr, Labprox, Labulti, Locate, Profile, Profinfo, SiteDNR, Siteinfo, TablesInPeat, VonPost) plus the MnGeo item 'about' page (captured as PDF) on 2026-09-15. No joins, corrections, or transformations applied to any raw file. Files relocated (git mv, no content changes) from data/mn_peat_inventory/ into the standard data/mn-peat-inventory/mn-peat-inventory--ing20260915--r001/raw/ layout on 2026-09-15; SHA-256 manifest generated with scripts/manifest.py after relocation.
notes: Source narrative states survey work began 1976 and reports/maps were published 1979-1982; Profinfo.csv Desc_when dates directly span 1971-08-02 to 2006-03-20 (excluding 3 apparent single-record data-entry anomalies: 'March 18, 1882', 'February 13, 2016', 'July 26, 2977' - not corrected here). Source narrative also states 'twenty Minnesota counties' and 'nine data tables'; Locate.csv shows 21 distinct counties, and TablesInPeat.csv enumerates only 7 tables against 10 data CSVs supplied (+ the catalog file itself). See REVIEW-QUESTIONS.txt in this release folder for the full list of items needing human review before this registration is finalized.

title: NASIS Pedon and Site Data Export for Minnesota (NCSS Pedon Schema 7.4.1)
abstract: 79,451 soil pedon records (point-based soil profile descriptions) with linked site, horizon, laboratory, taxonomic-history, vegetation-transect, and site-observation data, extracted from the USDA NRCS National Soil Information System (NASIS) for a Minnesota-focused area of interest. Delivered as three parallel representations of the same NASIS pedon/site query: an NCSS Pedon Schema 7.4.1 SQLite database (mn-nasis-export.sqlite; 93 tables per sqlite_master), an Esri file geodatabase point feature class with the same pedon attribute schema (mn-nasis-16DEC2024.gdb), and a companion point shapefile (tcms-nasis.shp*, WGS84). Source: mn-nasis-export_logFile.txt (extraction log) and tcms-nasis.shp.xml (feature-class lineage metadata).
source_org: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS); data drawn from the National Cooperative Soil Survey (NCSS) National Soil Information System (NASIS)
source_citation: Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. National Soil Information System (NASIS). Data exported for a Minnesota area of interest via the NCSS-Pedons ArcGIS Pro extraction tool (NCSS Pedon Schema 7.4.1); file geodatabase dated 2024-12-16, SQLite export dated 2025-01-13 (file timestamps). This citation string was constructed by the curator from general USDA/NASIS citation convention and delivery evidence; no verbatim 'cite this data as ...' string was supplied with the delivery -- see notes.
geo_description: Minnesota, selected by intersecting an initial rectangular lat/long bounding-box query against an 'mn-aoi-box' area-of-interest polygon (per mn-nasis-export_logFile.txt); the AOI polygon itself was not included in this delivery, so some pedons near the Minnesota border (in neighboring states/Ontario) may be included depending on the AOI's exact extent/buffer. Initial rectangular bounding-box query returned 86,076 candidate pedons; 79,451 intersected the AOI polygon and were delivered.
spatial_reference: WGS84 geographic coordinates (GCS_WGS_1984 / EPSG:4326), per tcms-nasis.shp.xml spatial-reference info and the source pedon feature-class template (NASISPedonsFGDBTemplate_NASIS_7_4_1.gdb).
intellectual_rights: mn-nasis-export_logFile.txt states the export tool attempted to delete attributes that may contain PII before delivery ('Deleting attributes that may contain PII information from the following fields'), but the log shows this step raised a Python KeyError for the main.siteobstext table ('KeyError: siteobstext') and did not complete for that table. The log's own captured error excerpts for main.siteobstext include apparent personal names in free-text fields (e.g. 'Lee Camp'). This delivery has NOT been confirmed free of PII in main.siteobstext (and possibly other free-text tables); treat as sensitive pending review -- see notes and REVIEW-QUESTIONS.txt. No formal license/rights statement was otherwise supplied with the delivery; NASIS soil survey data are generally treated as public USDA data, but that has not been independently confirmed for this export.
methods_summary: Standard NCSS (National Cooperative Soil Survey) pedon description methodology: point-based soil profile (pedon) descriptions with linked site descriptions, horizon-level morphology (color, texture, structure, fragments, roots, redoximorphic features, etc.), field-measured properties (bulk density, infiltration, penetration resistance), laboratory characterization data (NCSS/lab pedon and layer data), taxonomic classification history, vegetation transect composition, and site geomorphic/parent-material/hydric descriptions, recorded into NASIS by NRCS and NCSS-cooperating soil scientists over time. obsdate values in the siteobs table (Julian-date encoded) span 1900-12-14 to 2024-12-05 after excluding a small number of apparent data-entry anomalies -- see coverage note. Source: table/record structure and record counts in mn-nasis-export_logFile.txt; field definitions in the MetadataTable of mn-nasis-export.sqlite (NASIS data dictionary).
processing_summary: Lab (via NASIS user account referenced in the export log's Windows file paths as 'JELIN062') ran the public NCSS-Pedons ArcGIS Pro extraction tool (NASISpedons_Extract_Pedons_from_NASIS_MultiThreading_ArcGISPro_SQL.py) against NASIS web services for a Minnesota area of interest. The tool paged through 318 NASIS API requests and imported 79,451 pedons into a new NCSS Pedon Schema 7.4.1 SQLite database (mn-nasis-export.sqlite, file-dated 2025-01-13) and an Esri file geodatabase point feature class (mn-nasis-16DEC2024.gdb, geodatabase file-dated 2024-12-16); a companion point shapefile (tcms-nasis.shp*, file-dated 2025-02-07) was exported from the same feature class. Three malformed main.siteobstext source records (containing unescaped '|' delimiters within a text field in NASIS itself) were dropped by the extraction tool and reported in the log; total record counts elsewhere in the log (e.g. 79,451 pedons) are unaffected. A scripted PII-field-removal step failed for main.siteobstext specifically (Python KeyError) -- see intellectual_rights. No further joins, corrections, transformations, or PII remediation were applied by the lab. The three delivered artifacts (sqlite db, file geodatabase, shapefile) were moved unchanged (mv, no content changes) from an ad hoc upload path (data/NASIS/MN-NASIS/) into the standard data/mn-nasis-pedons--ing20260925--r001/raw/ layout on 2026-09-25, and two stray macOS .DS_Store files (not source content) were discarded during that move; SHA-256 manifest generated with scripts/manifest.py after the move. Given the raw delivery's size (~813 MB total, no git-lfs configured in this repository), raw/ contents for this release were added to a new repository .gitignore and are NOT committed to git; only this packages row, the manifest file, and .gitignore are version-controlled -- see notes.
notes: New dataset concept (first NASIS/pedon-type registration in this registry; distinct from the existing mn-peat-inventory dataset, which is DNR peatland survey data, not NASIS pedon data). Granularity: one packages row covers all three delivered representations (sqlite, gdb, shapefile) of what the export log describes as a single coordinated NASIS query/export event, unlike mn-peat-inventory's many independently-sourced per-table CSVs -- confirm this granularity is preferred over separate rows per artifact. mn-nasis-export_logFile.txt's own 'Bounding Box Coordinates' block labels the coordinates 'East Longitude: -97.79...' and 'West Longitude: -88.90...', which is geographically backwards for a Minnesota-area box (-97.79 is farther west than -88.90, matching Minnesota's real extent); west/east above were assigned by standard geographic convention (west = more negative) rather than the log's literal (apparently transposed) labels -- flagging the conflict rather than silently trusting either source. coverage_start/end exclude 28 of 79,451 siteobs.obsdate values that fall outside 1900-2025 (3 before 1900, as early as 1755-01-01; 25 after 2025, including a cluster of 19 records dated in 2096 and others as late as 6469-10-01) -- likely data-entry errors in NASIS itself, NOT corrected here; full obsdate range including these anomalies is 1755-01-01 to 6469-10-01. See REVIEW-QUESTIONS.txt in this release folder for the full list of items needing human review, including the unconfirmed 'JELIN062' identity, the siteobstext PII gap, and the git-lfs/.gitignore decision.

title: Minnesota DNR Relevé Database -- Site Data Export
abstract: 11,493 vegetation-survey plot ('relevé') site records from the Minnesota DNR Relevé Database, maintained by the DNR's Minnesota Biological Survey (MBS) program. Each record gives one plot's location (UTM Zone 15N NAD83 easting/northing and a PostGIS point geometry, EPSG:26915), lead surveyor, contributing institution, survey date, MNDNR Native Plant Community (NPC) classification (class/type/subtype, version 2.0), site environmental descriptors (slope, aspect, topographic position, litter/humus, soil texture, drainage class, bedrock depth, standing water depth/pH, earthworm presence), and free-text remarks. This is SITE DATA only, per the distinction drawn in the accompanying DNR Relevé Data Request and Data Use Agreement (which separately defines 'Species Data' -- per-plot species composition/cover -- as a different, not-included, request category). A companion field-level data dictionary (DNR releve site metadata_06-2018.xlsx) and the Data Use Agreement itself (ancillary information/) accompany the CSV.
source_org: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Minnesota Biological Survey (MBS) program; records also name 14 other contributing institutions (see notes)
source_citation: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources, Minnesota Biological Survey. Relevé Database site data export, downloaded 2024-11-05. Per the DNR Relevé Data Request and Data Use Agreement (revised June 2013): 'The user shall acknowledge the DNR's Minnesota Biological Survey Program as the source of the information in any product derived from the relevé dataset.' No separate formal 'cite this data as ...' string was supplied; this citation was constructed by the curator from the Data Use Agreement's acknowledgement requirement and the file/metadata evidence -- see notes.
geo_description: Primarily Minnesota: 9,048 of 11,493 records have state_code=MN, 2 have state_code=WI, and 2,443 have state_code=NA (missing); 88 distinct county_name values are represented (27 records have county_name=NA). Statewide MBS relevé vegetation-plot coverage rather than a single contiguous study area, per releve_site_export_20241105.csv.
spatial_reference: NAD83 / UTM Zone 15N (EPSG:26915) -- confirmed by decoding the PostGIS EWKB the_geom values (SRID 26915) and cross-checking against the utm_easting/utm_northing columns in releve_site_export_20241105.csv, which match exactly. NOT WGS84 decimal degrees; packages.west/east/south/north left blank pending a real coordinate transform (no GIS transform library was available in this environment) -- see REVIEW-QUESTIONS.txt, consistent with how mn-peat-inventory handled the same UTM/WGS84 gap.
intellectual_rights: raw/ancillary information/DNR Releve Data Use Agreement_2013.doc (a blank/unsigned request-form template, not a signed copy specific to this delivery) states binding terms for external use of relevé data: (1) the location or identity of any endangered, threatened, or special-concern plant species recorded in the data must be masked in any product for external distribution (identity masked to a term no more specific than genus, location masked to no finer than a Public Land Survey section); (2) the data must not be shared with any other party or transferred elsewhere without DNR's prior written consent; (3) any derived product must carry a copyright notice naming the DNR or the user; (4) any derived product must acknowledge the DNR's Minnesota Biological Survey Program as the source. license=nap because this is a restricted-use agreement, not an open/formal license. Whether the lab has an executed (signed) copy of this agreement on file with DNR for this specific 2024-11-05 export was NOT confirmed in this pass -- only the blank template form was included in the delivery. Treat this release as restricted-use pending that confirmation -- see REVIEW-QUESTIONS.txt.
methods_summary: Relevé (plot-based) vegetation survey methodology: field surveyors establish a plot (plot_length/width/area recorded), classify the native plant community present per the MNDNR Native Plant Community Classification version 2.0 (class/type/subtype, condition rank A-D per ecological integrity), and record site environmental descriptors (slope, aspect, topographic position, litter/humus depth and type, soil texture and drainage class, bedrock depth, standing-water depth and pH, earthworm presence/rank) and free-text remarks. Plots were contributed by 15 distinct institutions over 1964-2024 (see notes), coordinated/curated through the DNR's Minnesota Biological Survey program. Field descriptions in DNR releve site metadata_06-2018.xlsx (data dictionary, Sheet1, Field Name/Description/Valid Values columns); classification-scheme reference: 'MNDNR Native Plant Community Classification, version 2.0'. This export is SITE DATA only -- it does not include per-plot species composition/cover records (see abstract).
processing_summary: Lab received three files directly from DNR (Minnesota Biological Survey contact: Dan Wovcha, per the Data Use Agreement) or a DNR data steward: releve_site_export_20241105.csv (exported/downloaded 2024-11-05 per the CSV's own download_date column, uniform across all 11,493 rows), DNR releve site metadata_06-2018.xlsx (field-level data dictionary; created 2014-04-07 by Dan Wovcha, last modified 2024-11-05 by Amy Kendig (DNR) per the xlsx's own document properties -- the same date as the CSV download, suggesting but not confirming Kendig prepared this specific export), and DNR Releve Data Use Agreement_2013.doc (blank data-request/use-agreement template, revised June 2013). No joins, corrections, or transformations applied to any raw file. Files moved unchanged (mv, no content changes) from an ad hoc upload path (data/mn releve/raw/, containing a space, not kebab-case) into the standard data/mn-releve--ing20260925--r001/raw/ layout on 2026-09-25, and two stray macOS .DS_Store files (not source content) were discarded during that move; SHA-256 manifest generated with scripts/manifest.py after the move.
notes: New dataset concept (first Relevé/MBS vegetation-plot registration in this registry; distinct from mn-peat-inventory [DNR peatland survey] and mn-nasis-pedons [USDA NASIS soil pedons]). institution_name distribution across the 11,493 records: MBS-DNR 6,182; USFS-Chippewa NF 1,352; Univ. of Minnesota 1,115; NHP-DNR (DNR Natural Heritage Program) 712; Consultant 448; The Nature Conservancy 392; USFS-Superior NF 238; Other 217; National Park Service 172; Nat. Res. Res. Inst. 138; Environ. Qual. Bd - CuNi 81; Three Rivers Park District 68; NA 68; DNR-EWR 52; Pollution Control Agency 50; (plus a small remainder). Only mn-dnr (encompassing MBS-DNR, by far the largest single contributor and the party explicitly named as required-acknowledgement source in the Data Use Agreement) was credited with a party-role in this pass; the other ~14 contributing institutions were NOT registered as parties or credited -- see REVIEW-QUESTIONS.txt. 157 unique lead_surveyors_name values are present in the CSV (top contributor: Nancy P. Sather, 1,108 records); none were resolved to individual party records in this pass (unlike mn-peat-inventory, no corroborating external document -- e.g. a report title page -- was available here to disambiguate/confirm individual identities; the raw column alone was judged insufficient evidence) -- see REVIEW-QUESTIONS.txt. coverage_start=1964-01-01 is the literal minimum of the date_ column, but 258 of 11,493 records (2.2%) share that exact date and another 18 share 1977-01-01 -- January-1-of-a-round-year clusters this large are consistent with a placeholder/unknown-date convention rather than 258 independently confirmed survey dates; NOT corrected here. releve_status_name shows most records (8,108 of 11,493) as 'Transfer in Progress' rather than 'Quality Checked Complete' (3,285) or 'Publishable' (3) -- confirm whether 'Transfer in Progress' records should be treated as provisional/lower-confidence. See REVIEW-QUESTIONS.txt in this release folder for the full list of items needing human review before this registration is finalized.
